info.text:
Ecuador killed its own currency in 2000 at 25,000 sucres per dollar, and Panama has used the US dollar since 1904. This video explains dollarization in plain words: Panama's 1904 deal and its seven-day banknotes of 1941, Ecuador's 1998-2000 crisis (bank freeze, a collapsing sucre, 96.1% inflation in 2000), and what happened next. We cover El Salvador and its bitcoin law, Zimbabwe, Timor-Leste and the Pacific, the real trade-offs (low inflation versus no lender of last resort and rates set by the Fed), Argentina's debate, and what it means for savings, prices and remittances.
